haiku-low.q1: The old engine charges customers and writes the ledger. The new engine writes its invoices only to the shadow store.
haiku-low.q2: The new engine charges customers and writes the ledger. The old engine keeps computing every invoice into the shadow store, without charging.
haiku-low.q3: 7 consecutive days with mismatch rate under 0.1% and at least 5,000 invoices compared, read from comparison_results. A person asks the rollout tool to make the move.
haiku-low.q4: The billing monitor starts it automatically when the new engine's charge failure rate exceeds 2% over any 10-minute window, in both or new_only.
haiku-low.q5: Every rollback ends in old_only. Afterwards gates reset: the rollout must pass shadow again and the 7-day count starts over.
haiku-low.q6: From day 35 after new_only began, because the usage event log keeps only 35 days and the old engine must replay skipped events.
haiku-low.q8: Gate evidence is kept in comparison_results plus dates and stop point in the rollout tool; the tool refuses moves whose gate fails.
haiku-low.q9: The billing monitor watches the new engine's charge failure rate over any 10-minute window. Above 2%, it starts an automatic rollback.
haiku-low.q10: The charging-paused switch is on, so due charges are only delayed. Charging happens during reconcile, where a ledger entry lacking a provider charge is charged once.
haiku-low.q11: Catch_up keeps existing ledger entries so none are duplicated. Reconcile charges only ledger entries with no provider charge and flags any second provider charge.
haiku-low.q12: Billing is left with charging paused and the rollback record showing the failed step. The tool retries that step; if retries keep failing, it pages on-call.

sonnet.q1: The old engine charges and writes the ledger. The new engine reads the same usage events and writes its invoices only to the shadow store (never charges, never writes the ledger).
sonnet.q2: The new engine charges and writes the ledger. The old engine keeps computing every invoice into the shadow store, without charging, so it stays current.
sonnet.q3: 7 consecutive days with a mismatch rate under 0.1% and at least 5,000 invoices compared, read from comparison_results (after a rollback only rows dated after it finished count). A person asks the rollout tool for the move; the tool checks the gate and sets billing_mode.
sonnet.q4: The billing monitor starts one when the new-engine charge failure rate is above 2% over any 10-minute window. This applies in both and new_only (not in shadow). From day 35 in new_only it is refused and on-call is paged.
sonnet.q5: Every rollback ends in old_only. Before the new engine can take over again, the rollback record must close, and the rollout must go through shadow again, meeting the shadow-to-both gate with the 7-day count starting over from the rollback's finish.
sonnet.q6: From day 35 counted from the day new_only began. The usage event log keeps only 35 days and the old engine must replay skipped events, so from day 35 the oldest are gone.
sonnet.q8: Gate evidence is in comparison_results plus the last-rollback finish date, the date new_only began and the stop point (kept by the rollout tool); Finance sign-off is recorded in the rollout tool. The rollout tool refuses forward moves unless the gate passes (flag unchanged, names the failed condition); it also refuses to skip steps or move while a rollback record is open.
sonnet.q9: The billing monitor. It measures the new engine's charge failure rate (above 2% over any 10-minute window). When met, it starts an automatic rollback (in both or new_only); on day 35 or later in new_only the rollback is refused and it pages on-call.
sonnet.q10: Charging is paused (charging-paused switch is on, checked before every charge), so due charges are only delayed. They are made in the reconcile step: a ledger entry with no provider charge is charged once. Charging resumes after resume_charging.
sonnet.q11: The ledger is the system of record and has at most one entry per customer and billing period. catch_up keeps entries the new engine already wrote and writes only where none exists. Reconcile compares ledger to the payment provider; a ledger entry with a provider charge is not charged again, and a second provider charge is flagged for a person (no automatic refunds). Charging is also paused during the rollback.
sonnet.q12: Charging stays paused until the rollback finishes. The tool retries the failed step using the rollback record (current step and done steps); if retries keep failing, it pages on-call. Retry count and delay are not decided.
